body:
## Summary
kp's collision authority for its own interviews is exact-instant equality, but the pool it guards now holds off-grid minutes (grid picks, accepted proposals) and per-invite durations. Move ONE overlap predicate - real-duration interval OR same interview-zone hour - into the store's `.immediate()` transactions and the slot proposer, and delete the single route-level hour-bucket pre-read.

## Description
`confirmScheduleInvite` and `rescheduleScheduleInvite` refuse a booking only when another confirmed invite has the *identical* `slot_at` (schedule-store.ts:432, :557), and `proposeSlots` hides a time only on the same equality (schedule-slots.ts:179/194). That was sound when every booking sat on the fixed `KP_INTERVIEW_TIMES` grid at 45 minutes. It is not any more: `dateSlotToIso` books any minute from the week grid, `proposedSlotFor` accepts any working minute, and `duration_min` varies per invite (22-min student screen, 90-min spans pinned in calendar-conflict.test.ts). The code already knows: `hourBucketKey`'s doc says the store 'wouldn't catch this', and a patch lives in exactly one handler (route.ts:228-233, the grid `book`), as a non-transactional read. `accept_proposal`, recruiter reschedule, and the candidate token confirm/reschedule all book a 14:30 beside a 14:00, and a 90-minute 14:00 beside a 15:00. Only a connected Google calendar masks it (kp's own event shows as busy to `slotStillFree`); the keyless/not-connected default has no guard at all.

The move: a pure `bookingCollides(candidate, existing[], tz)` in schedule-slots.ts (half-open real interval using each row's `duration_min ?? DEFAULT_INTERVIEW_MINUTES`, OR same `hourBucketKey`), called inside both store transactions against the workspace's confirmed rows in a +/- 1 day window, and by `proposeSlots` via a `bookedIntervals()` read. The route's bucket pre-read is deleted; the store's `taken` becomes the one refusal.

## Flow
1. Write schedule-collision.test.ts cases 1-6 against the pure predicate and the store (isolated KP_DB_PATH, as schedule-store.test.ts does) - all fail today.
2. Add `bookingCollides` + `bookedIntervals()`; keep `bookedSlots()` string output for existing callers.
3. Replace the equality SELECT in both transactions with SELECT slot_at, duration_min ... then `bookingCollides` - still synchronous, still inside `.immediate()`, compensating WHERE preconditions untouched.
4. `proposeSlots` accepts intervals (strings still accepted); `proposeFreeSlots` and the two token-route callers pass `bookedIntervals(ws)`.
5. Delete route.ts:228-233; add the accept_proposal route case (7) to the existing refusals test.
6. Update docs/features/scheduling/README.md (collision authority section + Known gaps).

## Expected impact
Closes a silent double-booking class on every path except the one that happened to be patched, for every deployment without Google connected; turns a documented admission ('wouldn't catch this') into an enforced invariant held in one place and inside the lock rather than in a TOCTOU pre-read. Makes a future per-interviewer pool (the open L backlog item) an extra key on one predicate instead of five handler edits.

## Evaluation
Claim: every booking path refuses an overlapping own-booking, and the proposer never offers one.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: contract (node:test - new schedule-collision.test.ts + the existing schedule refusals tests, run by npm run test:unit)
Result: pending build
Gate: contract

title: Turn a revoked Google grant from a silent 'unavailable' into Reconnect now
acceptance: refreshAccessToken rejects with Google error 'invalid_grant' during fetchBusy -> getCalendarConnection(ws).health === 'revoked' and healthAt is set
health 'revoked': fetchBusy / createInterviewEvent make ZERO fetch calls (mocked fetch counter stays 0) and return their 'no information' values - no 8s token round trip per candidate page load

proposeFreeSlots on a revoked grant -> calendarStatus 'needs_reconnect'; on a healthy grant whose free/busy call answers 503 twice -> still 'unavailable' (a transient outage never marks the grant revoked)
a stored token that no longer decrypts (at-rest key rotated) -> health 'undecryptable' -> calendarStatus 'needs_reconnect'
saveCalendarConnection after a successful re-consent -> health back to 'ok', healthAt cleared

rollback: Additive: two nullable columns on calendar_connections (added via ALTER in token-store's db()), one CalendarStatus member, one optional GoogleOAuthError.code, catalog keys appended. Reverting the commit series leaves harmless unused columns; a 'revoked' row simply reads as connected again, i.e. today's behaviour.
runner_up: Tell the candidate when a recruiter cancels or accepts their proposed time - POST /api/schedule cancel/accept_proposal dispatch no candidate mail and eventBody deliberately omits sendUpdates, so the candidate learns only from the reminder.
body:
## Summary
When Google revokes kp's grant, kp keeps saying 'Connected', keeps calling Google on every candidate page load, and tells the recruiter 'could not check your calendar' as if it were a blip. Persist the grant's health, stop calling a dead grant, and turn the status into the one action that fixes it: Reconnect, with how many upcoming interviews never reached the calendar.

## Description
A revoked or undecryptable grant is the chronic failure the governing subject names, and kp renders it as the transient one. `accessTokenFor` logs `invalid_grant` and returns null (google-calendar.ts:67-76); `connected` is just `!!refresh_token` (token-store.ts:99); `proposeFreeSlots` maps every connected-but-silent case to `unavailable` (available-slots.ts:65). The Integrations panel shows a healthy connection card with no Reconnect (IntegrationsCalendarPanel.tsx:117-134), the Schedule tab's status offers no action for `unavailable` (ScheduleCalendarStatus.tsx:26), and every booking quietly records `calendar_event_state = 'failed'`. Meanwhile each public page load spends a token round trip on a grant that cannot recover.

The leap: `GoogleOAuthError` carries Google's `error` code; `accessTokenFor` records `health = 'revoked'` on `invalid_grant` and `'undecryptable'` on a decrypt throw (never on timeouts/5xx), and short-circuits while unhealthy; `saveCalendarConnection` resets to `ok`. `CALENDAR_STATUSES` gains `needs_reconnect` (recruiter-only - the candidate wire stays one bit). The panel shows 'Google stopped accepting kp's access on <date>' with a Reconnect button and 'N upcoming interviews are not on your calendar'; the Schedule tab status links Reconnect for `needs_reconnect`.

## Flow
1. Write grant-health.test.ts cases 1-6 (mock fetch, isolated KP_DB_PATH) - all fail today.
2. token-store: ALTER-add `health`, `health_at`; expose `health` on CalendarConnection; `markCalendarHealth(ws, state)`; reset in saveCalendarConnection.
3. google-oauth: `GoogleOAuthError.code` from `o.error`. google-calendar: record + short-circuit in accessTokenFor; readStoredToken marks 'undecryptable'.
4. free-busy: add `needs_reconnect` to CALENDAR_STATUSES; available-slots: unchecked status reads health.
5. schedule-store: `countUnsyncedUpcomingInvites(ws)` (workspace-scoped, future confirmed, state 'failed'); route GET returns it.
6. Panel + ScheduleCalendarStatus render the actionable state; catalog keys appended to all four locales (no em dashes); doc updated.

## Expected impact
A recruiter learns about a dead calendar the day it dies instead of after the first double-booking; the fix is one click where the problem is shown. Removes a per-request Google round trip from the public booking page for every workspace with a revoked grant, and makes the 'failed' event chips explicable (they have a named cause and a count).

## Evaluation
Claim: a revoked/undecryptable grant is persisted, stops network calls, and surfaces as an actionable needs_reconnect with the affected-interview count.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: contract (node:test - grant-health.test.ts, google-calendar.test.ts, calendar-status-i18n.test.ts via npm run test:unit; i18n:check for catalog parity)
Result: pending build
Gate: none
